facts.raw_span: intensely pruritic skin lesions on her anterior thighs
lesions first appeared 2 weeks earlier in recurrent 3‐day outbreaks
resolved spontaneously without residual injury
well‐defined, confluent, erythematous papules and plaques with annular, arciform, and polycyclic morphology
central clearing, and purpuric edges
symmetrically distributed on the anterior thighs in a mirror‐image pattern
no systemic symptoms
no preceding infection
laboratory studies were within normal limits

complete blood count, biochemistry, urinalysis, erythrocyte sedimentation rate, C‐reactive protein, complement levels (C3, C4, C1q), immunoglobulin levels, rheumatoid factor, and acute‐phase reactants were within normal limits
Antinuclear, anti–double‐stranded DNA, antineutrophil cytoplasmic, anti–Ro, anti–La, and transglutaminase antibodies were negative
Serologies for syphilis, hepatitis B and C viruses, HIV, cytomegalovirus, Epstein–Barr virus, and parvovirus B19 were negative

concepts.why: The patient presents with intensely pruritic skin lesions that are well-defined, confluent, erythematous papules and plaques with annular, arciform, and polycyclic morphology, which is consistent with urticaria.
The patient's skin lesions have a characteristic annular, arciform, and polycyclic morphology with central clearing and purpuric edges, which is consistent with erythema annulare centrifugum.
The patient presents with intensely pruritic skin lesions that are well-defined, confluent, erythematous papules and plaques, which is consistent with pityriasis rosea.
The patient's skin lesions are symmetrically distributed on the anterior thighs in a mirror-image pattern, which is consistent with nummular dermatitis.
The patient presents with intensely pruritic skin lesions, which could be consistent with contact dermatitis.
The patient's skin lesions are intensely pruritic, which is consistent with atopic dermatitis.
The patient's skin lesions have a characteristic morphology with well-defined, confluent, erythematous papules and plaques, which is consistent with psoriasis.
The patient's skin lesions have a characteristic morphology with well-defined, confluent, erythematous papules and plaques, which is consistent with lichen planus.
The patient presents with intensely pruritic skin lesions, which could be consistent with dermatitis herpetiformis.
The patient's skin lesions have a characteristic morphology with well-defined, confluent, erythematous papules and plaques, which is consistent with erythema multiforme.

rationales.F06: Symmetric distribution in a mirror-image pattern is characteristic of several dermatological conditions.
